title: Frenchton: French Bulldog × Boston Terrier Mix Health Facts
description: What a Frenchton is, how it compares with a Frenchie, the health issues both parent breeds pass on, and what is still unknown about Frenchton lifespan.
secondaryKeywords: frenchton how big do they get
keywordEs: frenchton (cruce entre bulldog francés y boston terrier)

faq.q: Is a Frenchton a real breed?
faq.a: No. A Frenchton is a French Bulldog and Boston Terrier cross with no breed standard or breed club. The AKC handles mixed breeds through an enrollment program, not breed registration.

faq.q: Are Frenchtons healthier than French Bulldogs?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Both parent breeds have flat faces and can share inherited risks. A study of other designer crosses cannot establish the health of Frenchtons specifically; evaluate each parent and puppy.

No reliable Frenchton-specific population lifespan estimate was identified in this audit. Figures quoted by sellers should not be treated as established life expectancy. Parent-breed data do not predict an individual crossbred dog's lifespan.
There is no standardized Frenchton size. Adult size varies with the parents and genetics, so the parent breeds' size standards are only rough context, not a promise about a puppy.

faq.q: What health tests should a Frenchton breeder do?
faq.a: Ask for each parent's breathing grade, eye exam by a veterinary ophthalmologist, HSF4 juvenile cataract DNA result, and hip, kneecap and heart screening.
